cards.text: The Lord GOD has been showing Amos visions, and the last one ends with the Lord rising up against the house of Jeroboam with His sword (Amos 7:9). Now Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sends word to Jeroboam king of Israel. And friend, this is NOT a thank-you note.

cards.question: In his message to King Jeroboam, what does Amaziah the priest accuse Amos of?

cards.text: Then Amaziah adds, "The land cannot bear all his words." The LAND, friend. Not "I'm a little annoyed." The whole COUNTRY needs to go lie down.

cards.question: Amaziah tells the king that Amos said Jeroboam will die by the ___.
Amaziah also reports that Amos said Israel will go into exile, away from their homeland.

cards.text: Then Amaziah turns to Amos himself: "Go away, you seer!" No hello. No "how was your trip." Just GO. GO. GO!

cards.question: Amaziah tells Amos to flee somewhere else. Where?

cards.text: Earn your bread there, Amaziah says, and do your prophesying there. But never prophesy at Bethel again.

cards.question: Amaziah says Amos can never prophesy at Bethel again, because it is the sanctuary of the ___.

cards.text: Now Amos answers. And he opens with his résumé. Short résumé. One page. Big font.

cards.question: Amos tells Amaziah he was a prophet and the son of a prophet.
So what was Amos doing before he ever showed up at Bethel?

cards.text: Then Amos says, "But the LORD took me from following the flock." Friend, I RELATE. One day you're a 25-cent stamper under a pile of takeout menus. Next day you've got a gold base and a JOB.

cards.question: When the LORD took Amos from the flock, He told him, Go ___ to My people Israel.

cards.text: Then Amos turns it all the way around: "Now, therefore, hear the word of the LORD." Amaziah wanted Amos to stop talking. Now the LORD has a word for Amaziah.

cards.question: Amos says Amaziah is the one telling him not to prophesy against Israel.

cards.text: "Therefore this is what the LORD says." Amaziah's wife will become a prostitute in the city, and his sons and daughters will fall by the sword.

cards.question: The LORD also says Amaziah's land will be divided. What will divide it?
And what does the LORD say will happen to Amaziah himself?

answers.text: He will die on pagan soil

cards.text: Then the word closes with that line again: "Israel will surely go into exile, away from their homeland." Amaziah told Amos to go away and stay quiet. Friend, the herdsman just delivered the LORD's word right there at Bethel.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card says the Lord rises up against the house of Jeroboam 'with His sword' (Amos 7:9). This gives away the answer to card 4, which asks the baker to fill in that Jeroboam will die by the 'sword'.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Amos appears here for the first time but is never introduced. The card names Amaziah as priest of Bethel and Jeroboam as king of Israel, but it never says simply who Amos is (a prophet).

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question types repeat in a fixed cycle: multiple choice, fill in the blank, true or false, three times in a row (cards 2, 4, 5, then 7, 9, 11, then 12, 14, 16), before ending on two multiple choice cards.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: Card 10's setup joke ('Short résumé. One page. Big font.') tells the baker that Amos's background is modest. That rules out the two prestigious wrong answers, 'Writing in the king's court' and 'Serving as a temple priest', and leaves only the humble right answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke calls back 'a 25-cent stamper under a pile of takeout menus' but never says this was the junk drawer. Takeout menus are one of the drawer's small details, so a baker may not catch the reference.

rule.text: Bakers know he spent years in a junk drawer, from onboarding. The drawer's small details, like the batteries, the key or the coupon, only come up when the line says what they are, like "the dead batteries I shared that drawer with."

findings.problem: The card says 'Amaziah wanted Amos to stop talking.' The text does not say this. In Amos 7:12-13, Amaziah tells Amos to go do his prophesying in Judah and only forbids him from prophesying at Bethel.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: This true or false card asks whether Amaziah is the one telling Amos not to prophesy against Israel. Card 15, right before it, already says Amaziah wanted Amos to stop talking, and card 8 already told Amaziah's order. The answer is given away.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'He will rule over Bethel' is a reward, while the question sits in a list of judgments. Its tone doesn't match the other answers, which makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card says 'Amaziah told Amos to go away and stay quiet.' Amos 7:12 shows the opposite: Amaziah tells Amos to 'do your prophesying there' in Judah. He only forbids prophesying at Bethel (Amos 7:13).

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
